To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aortic occlusion in the cat results in the development of a collateral circulation that can restore blood flow to the distal aorta and hindlimbs.
the development of collateral blood vessels in the cat hindlimb following experimental aortic occlusion depends on the type of occlusion.

1) the 5th lumbral artery appears to be an important origin of collateral vessels; 2) the mid-zone component is a dorsal vertebral, ventral vertebral, and epaxial muscle routes; 3) the re-entry component is the 6th and 7th lumbral arteries; 4) the collateral vessels arise from the pre-existing collateral vessels; 5) a thrombus inhibits collateral vessel development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of collateral blood flow to the hindlimb of the feline following aortic occlusion.
the development of collateral blood vessels and their role in maintaining blood flow to the hindlimb following experimental aortic occlusion.

the development of collateral vessels in the cat following acute occlusion of terminal aorta by ligature, thrombus formation and formation of a closed aortic loop containing a thromboplastin solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a thrombus in the terminal aorta is a significant inhibitory factor in the development of collateral blood flow to the hindlimbs.
a thrombus in the aortic lumen inhibits development of collateral circulation, whereas ligation of the aorta does not.
thrombosis in the aortic lumen inhibits collateral vessel development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of collateral blood vessels is inhibited when the occluding thrombus is present.
the development of collateral vessels is a rapid process and that thrombus formation inhibits the development of collateral blood vessels.
the presence of thrombus formation in the aortic ligation model inhibits the development of collateral vessels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of collateral vessels is a dynamic process.
the development of collateral vessels is not an all or none phenomenon.
the thrombus inhibits development of collateral circulation, and that the inhibition is not the result of the occlusion of the aorta.
